I've stopped. Nothing has been committed or pushed since the last checkpoint.

Where things stand

  • Branch: the local checkpoint commit 53299f80 (condensed into ae22657) sits on the improvement branch (9317d670 (condensed into 8251007)), with the edits below uncommitted on top. The remote branch still holds the older main-based commits, so the eventual push will need --force-with-lease.
  • Done since the checkpoint:
    • Eigen- and singular-value decompositions now always run on one thread. On this 4-CPU host, parallel eig was slower or no faster than one thread up to n = 512, and only 1.3× faster at n = 768. Parallel SVD was at most 1.7× faster, at n = 768. Both gave different results at different thread counts: eig from n = 64, SVD from n = 384. With one thread, diff.eig returns eigenvalues in the same order at every thread count, with no change to the API.
    • Changelog entries written for the new Python module, the native bindings, the Rust core, the docs, tooling, and the fixes: the fork hang, wrong reduce/accumulate results, unparsable thread settings silently using every CPU, and results that changed with the thread count.
    • Repo-rule fixes: the fork-hook binding now uses the required ieee(|| ...) form, parallel.py keeps its imports private, the three texts that state where unsafe code is allowed now name the threadpoolctl symbol, and docs that called the pool Rayon's are updated.
    • One-thread CI job at no extra cost: Python 3.12 runs the suite with TREAMS_RS_NUM_THREADS=1, and 3.13 uses every CPU.
    • Test fixes: the thread-name test now waits for workers to start, since it failed when they started late. The budget-1 expectation in the process-pool test now accepts the one-worker pool that cluster code still starts. The qualify-references test no longer leaves the thread budget changed for later tests.
    • The docs, scripts, float-environment, namespace and parallel API tests pass on the earlier release build.
  • Still running: the two background agents, one making gradient sums deterministic and one turning refused allocations into MemoryError. They are working in .claude/worktrees/ and keep going unless I stop them. The release rebuild with the current tree has also just finished.
  • Not done yet: merge the agents' work, rebuild, run the full Rust and Python checks, regenerate the docs, review, commit, and push.
